chapter: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
title: Lionel Hampton years, Mingus Fingers and the bebop song
summary: Hampton and Red Norvo were the longest jobs; tunes written for Hampton, lost in a bus wreck, and a bebop lyric Hampton disliked.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Lionel Hampton is about the longest, or Red Norvel.
Red Norvel, yeah. What else did you write for Lionel Hampton, besides Mingus Fingers?

Quite a few tunes with him. He said all that stuff was lost in the bus wreck. What was -- the names [BEBOPS -- see insert] I don't know. Some ballads. One was called (singing). I had this whole thing I wrote out. (Unintelligible) a little thing about bebop. And Lionel didn't want bebop. He said, "Hey, bobba rebop. It's rebop, not bebop." He says, "I made that up." Or he stole the tune.

Insert to page 31,
Mingus / Johnson interview.

" Bebop's taking over ca-ee.
Better bop while you're able to see
Open up your ears
Bop's been here for years
You really should be listening
It's time for bebop's christening.

Look here at the Down Beat press
Look at what this writer says
Bebop's the king
Bebop's the queen
You really should be listening
It's time for bebop's christening."
So he came up and rehearsed the band while Bebop was on '15 Taking over."
Did you have the whole band sing it?
(Singing.) I had the whole thing out there. The arrangement was good, too, man, kind of like Stravinsky -- I mean, like Boyd Raeburn and Duke at the same time.
Well, I remember when I heard Mingus Fingers for the first time, about -- I think it was Decca or something.

And it was a single, I don't remember what was on the other side of it. But it absolutely knocked me out. Totally blew my mind. It was the first time I had ever heard your name. And then, -- how long were you with Hampton?
At least a couple of years, maybe a year and a half, at least.
